impact: Per Pillar: a Gemini CLI triage flaw could lead to compromise of GCP project credentials and Editor-level access in a triage sandbox, with other users of the same reusable setup flow potentially exposed. Proof-of-concept; Google fixed it; no observed third-party exploitation.
mitigations: Google tightened agent tool scoping, blocked the agent from the sensitive credentials file, and narrowed a project-wide IAM role to a single service-account resource.
name: Pillar: a GitHub issue on Gemini CLI could lead to compromise of a GCP triage project

sources.title: A WIF Of Fresh Access: How a GitHub Issue on Gemini-CLI Led to GCP Project Compromise

summary: Pillar Security disclosed on 2026-08-18, through Google's vulnerability reward program, that a flaw in the Gemini CLI triage automation could lead to compromise of Google Cloud Platform project credentials and Editor-level access within the affected project, described by Google as a dedicated sandbox used for Gemini CLI triage automation. Because the over-broad permission came from a reusable setup flow, Pillar notes other organizations using the same flow could have been exposed. Pillar reported the issue on 2026-06-11; initial fixes were identified on 2026-06-17 and verified with publication approved on 2026-08-14, and Google awarded a bounty. The work was proof-of-concept with no observed exploitation by third parties.
